findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "readSource" is 825 chars, far longer than this server's median (130). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, readSource, submitFeedback · Private data: fetch, draftContactMessage, datasetChanges, identifyUserAgent, submitFeedback · Public sink: draftContactMessage, planAgentRetrieval, auditAgentDiscovery, actionPreflight, verifyApprovedAction, textStats, canonicalizeJson, readSource, submitFeedback · Destructive: readSource.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, readSource, submitFeedback · Private data: fetch, draftContactMessage, datasetChanges, identifyUserAgent, submitFeedback · Public sink: draftContactMessage, planAgentRetrieval, auditAgentDiscovery, actionPreflight, verifyApprovedAction, textStats, canonicalizeJson, readSource, submitFeedback · Destructive: readSource

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
